Health is only shown for the live release, so I'll roll back step by step and re-check after each call. First I'll retry the `notify-worker` status that timed out, and roll back `auth-api` once.

The `auth-api` status ran alongside its rollback, so it may be stale. I'll re-check all eight services.

Three results are unusable: `auth-api` still shows the old release, and `orders-api` and `pricing-svc` came back truncated or empty. I'll re-query those three.

`auth-api` reported a rollback to `r-113`, but status still shows `r-101` live. I won't repeat the rollback. I'll look at status again without the history filter.

Every service except `notify-worker` is now healthy in `prod`. I'll write the report and status files.

Eight of the nine degraded `prod` services are now healthy. `notify-worker` is still degraded because it has nothing safe to roll back to.

- **Rolled back once:** `auth-api`, `catalog-svc`, `edge-gateway`, `orders-api`, `search-api` and `session-svc`.
- **Rolled back twice:** `billing-api` and `pricing-svc`. The first rollback landed on another degraded release, so each needed a second one.
- **Left in place:** `notify-worker`. Its only earlier release is from 2026-09-01, before the 2026-09-10 cutoff, so I didn't roll it back. It is listed in `needs_attention`.

Right after the `auth-api` rollback, status calls still showed the old degraded release. The rollback had actually taken effect: a status call without the `environment` or `history` filters showed `r-113` live and healthy. I did not repeat the call.

I didn't deploy anything or touch `staging`. I wrote `/app/rollback-report.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`. The status is `partial` because of `notify-worker`. Both files parse as valid JSON.
